France has 74 divisions in 1936, but many of those are colonial divisions with only six infantry battalions, and their armored divisions are basically brigades.

France relies on the heavy fortifications at the border with ⟦0⟧, the ⟦1⟧ to defend them. With its far-flung and vast colonial possessions, defending them against attack will require a higher concentration of light, fast forces compared to Metropole defense.

In terms of technology, France has a good head start on mechanized, motorized and tank forces with only a little catch-up for infantry weapons. The problem with fielding a modern army will be expanding France's production base, which is both extremely limited and faced with the prospect of crippling manpower shortages in the very near future in 1936.
* marks a division that is removed in the 1939 start. ^ marks a division that is only available in the 1939 start.
* marks a variant as "outdated". ^ marks a variant that is only available in the 1939 start.

France boasts a somewhat modern - if badly understrength - fleet. Whilst the Marine Nationale is strong enough to decisively defeat either the ⟦0⟧ or the ⟦1⟧ alone, it would have no chance against a combined Axis fleet. As with her tanks, France begins the game with modern naval technology, such as 1936 BB, DD and SS techs and two unique designs: La Fantasque, a destroyer model with tier 3 (1940) engines, and the Surcouf Class cruiser submarine. Many of these designs are clearly aimed against an anti-surface role, prioritizing fast, lightly-armored ships with minimal ASW capability and strong scouting capabilities. However, poor naval infrastructure and low shipbuilding priority means that constructing a large modern fleet is not easy, and in fact can often be counter-productive in that it denies vital industrial capacity from tank and motorized production.

The below is ⟦0⟧ player suggested strategies for ⟦1⟧. Bear in mind, due to the dynamic nature of the game, it may unfold differently for other players.

Historically, France elected to ⟦0⟧, the left-wing Democratic path. This puts Léon Blum in power and unlocks ⟦1⟧ plus six more focuses that improve the economy and add free factories. Note that the Matignon Agreements can be repealed later for 50 PP but no other penalty. The right-wing Democratic path via ⟦2⟧ focuses on market reforms to fix the economy. Either way the priority is to get rid of your starting national spirits as soon as possible, especially Disjointed Government. Getting to ⟦3⟧ requires at least 350 days, or up to 490 via Revive the National Bloc and ⟦4⟧. A year after taking ⟦5⟧, you can take ⟦6⟧ to finally remove Disjointed Government. This means France will be starved for political power until 1938.

For your military, France's 18-width 'Division d'Infanterie' is good, though support anti-air is a good addition. The mountaineers and motorized infantry are also useful, but everything else can be converted to regular infantry. Medium tank divisions can be useful for encirclements but the limited military industry means you can't build more than a few armored divisions. A railway gun can be helpful for defending on the Belgian border and pushing back into Germany. Finally, building a lot of 1936 fighters is the only real counter to Germany's huge air force. The naval game isn't especially relevant as Germany is unable to construct a substantial surface fleet and Britain is capable of subduing the Regia Marina in the Mediterranean. As far as strategy goes, let your enemies attack without counterattacking, then push only when your troops are at full strength while your enemies are down to 75% or so.

If you go to war over Poland in mid-1939, the Axis can attack through three fronts: Alsace-Lorraine, Belgium after Germany conquers them, and Italy after they join Germany's faction. None of your other territory really matters, though you can place small forces to hold Corsica and Tunisia from the Italians. Alsace-Lorraine has level 10 forts so the Germans can't make any progress against two infantry divisions per tile. Belgium is dangerous because of the open terrain and the huge force that Germany will send this way. One option is to build forts to level 2 or 3 and then get ⟦0⟧ to add 2 more forts to each tile. The Italian front has good defensive terrain and a weaker foe but supply is bad in Savoy, so two good choices are to build a supply hub close to the Italian border or to entrench a few tiles to the west, letting the Italians advance a little way into the unsupplied area.

If you ⟦0⟧ instead of joining the Allies, the war is likely to start in mid-1938 instead. This version of the war may be easier because you won't face trouble on the Belgian or Italian fronts and the Germans will be bogged down attacking ⟦1⟧. If instead France joins no factions they won't be called in for the attack on Poland but Germany will still attack in 1940.

Release all occupied lands as ⟦0⟧ in ways that would result in as many tiny states as possible. All in all it will result in more manpower - on 1936, it's going from 274.51K to 309.40K once everything is released while keeping cores. And that's just French soldiers alone; you could then make colonial divisions to steal manpower of puppets, and request control of their divisions. Just check what country has how much manpower; for example, ⟦1⟧ has lots of manpower. If we factor in ⟦2⟧ puppet, that's a lot of manpower to use. Keep in mind what Manpower of France is more valuable and less replaceable than manpower of various "banana republics". Once manpower of one of ⟦3⟧ starts running low (gets to about 10-20K) - switch to another ⟦4⟧ to drain; once ⟦5⟧ of them are dangerously low - start draining them to zero. Use actual fully-french divisions as last resort.

These puppets will also complete ⟦0⟧; they would build up themselves, so you could focus industrial efforts as France. Releasing them earlier (or immediately) will allow for more build-up - but their templates will be starting ones, meaning crap divisions, what would in turn screw with "Steal manpower" plan. You can duplicate and edit templates of said Puppets - but you need ⟦1⟧ for that, and each Puppet has it's own templates.
⟦0⟧ should release ⟦1⟧ before ⟦2⟧ does so - make ⟦3⟧ waste a little bit more of manpower. ⟦4⟧ can't normally release ⟦5⟧, so that's not an issue.
Release 1-state puppets first. Divide territories into as many tiny puppets as possible. E.G. ⟦0⟧ must be released before ⟦1⟧.

The only problem, is that, likely, if France capitulates, the Free France wouldn't have direct control of ⟦0⟧ banana republics. As such, ⟦1⟧, colonies should be kept directly. However, it's a lot easier to hold off mainland France without capitulating, than it is to re-capture mainland France and launch counter-offensive against Axis as Free France; as such, non-capitulation plan is preferable, and for it the puppet strategy is preferable.
